test_title: PYST 26: RRB Group D - GA (Held On: 09 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following became India’s 107th National Park in April 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Similipal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In April 2025, the Odisha government officially notified Similipal as India's 107th National Park.
 
• It became the second national park in the state of Odisha, joining Bhitarkanika which was established in 1998.
 
• Melanistic Tigers: It is the world’s only natural habitat for pseudo-melanistic tigers, characterized by thick black stripes that almost cover their tawny coats.
 
• Biodiversity: The park is home to a significant population of Bengal tigers, Asian elephants, and over 94 species of orchids.
 
• Conservation Status: While it has been a Tiger Reserve since 1973 and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve since 2009, the new designation provides the highest level of legal protection under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gorumara National Park (West Bengal):**

 
 
• Located in the **Dooars region** at the foothills of the **Eastern Himalayas**, it lies on the floodplains of the **Murti River** and **Jaldhaka River**.
 
• The park is primarily known for the **Great Indian One-horned Rhinoceros**, **Asian Elephant**, and **Malayan Giant Squirrel**.
 
• The vegetation consists of **Tropical Moist Deciduous forests**, predominantly featuring **Sal** (Shorea robusta), **Teak**, and **Silk Cotton trees**.
 
 
 
• **Similipal National Park (Odisha):**
 
 
• It derives its name from the **Semul** (Red Silk Cotton) trees that bloom abundantly in the region.
 
• The area was formally designated a **Tiger Reserve** in **1956** and under **Project Tiger** in **May 1973**.
 
• It serves as a vital habitat for the **Bengal Tiger** and **Wild Buffalo**, covering an area of approximately **2,750 square kilometers**.
 
 
 
• **Dudhwa National Park (Uttar Pradesh):**
 
 
• It is a part of the **Dudhwa-Katerniaghat-Kishanpur** landscape, which forms one of the most important **Tiger Conservation Units** in India.
 
• The park was established as a result of the efforts of **Billy Arjan Singh**, a renowned conservationist.
 
• It is one of the few places in India where **one-horned rhinoceros** were successfully reintroduced in **1984**.
 
 
 
• **Bhitarkanika National Park (Odisha):**
 
 
• Surrounded by the **Brahmani**, **Baitarani**, and **Dhamra** rivers, it is the second-largest **mangrove ecosystem** in India after the Sundarbans.
 
• The park is home to the **Olive Ridley Sea Turtles**, which nest on the nearby **Gahirmatha Beach**.
 
• It contains **estuarine crocodiles**, **water monitor lizards**, and over **215 species of birds**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **National Parks in India:**

 
 
• Under the **Wildlife Protection Act, 1972**, the **State Government** has the power to declare an area as a National Park if it is considered of adequate ecological, faunal, floral, or geomorphological importance.
 
• No human activity is permitted inside a National Park except for those sanctioned by the **Chief Wildlife Warden** of the state.
 
• As of **2025**, the number of national parks has grown significantly to **107** to protect India’s diverse **biodiversity** and **endangered species**.
 
• The **first National Park** established in India was the **Hailey National Park** (now known as **Jim Corbett National Park**) in **1936** in the state of **Uttarakhand**.
